response.title: A Fair for Every Reader
response.passage:
Our school library held a book fair in the gym to raise money for new reading lamps. Students brought gently used books from home, and the library staff checked each one for torn pages or missing covers. On Thursday, the helpers arranged the books by age group so visitors could find stories that suited them. Several younger classes had asked to visit, so the organizers set aside a small selection for them. For next week's reading visit, the club decided to reserve six storybooks in a separate box. A bright label on that box helped the teachers find the books when their classes arrived.

The fair opened on Friday afternoon, just after the last class ended. The timetable was posted beside the gym doors, and every class had a short visit before students could shop freely. The current schedule gives each class only fifteen minutes at the display. Because it was so tight, the student guides prepared a quick tour and pointed visitors toward the right shelves. This plan helped the younger students choose books without making the line grow too long.

By noon, a shortage of helpers had become clear at the busiest table. To cover it, two students left the checkout desk and took turns answering questions there. A teacher watched the desk while they were away, so buyers could still pay without waiting too long. Meanwhile, another group wrote down the names of books that sold out, giving the librarian a clear list for future orders. Although the gym became noisy, the helpers kept the aisles open and reminded visitors to carry books carefully.

When the fair ended, the students counted the money and returned the unsold books to the library. They also checked the gym floor for price tags and paper scraps before leaving. The librarian compared the sales list with the books still on the shelves. That comparison showed which kinds of stories had attracted the most interest. The school used the results to choose new titles, and the students felt proud that their careful work would help more classmates enjoy reading.
